retoken: keyword 74 DSCR (Macross 7 song energy): 'Dr. $$千葉$$' -> 'Dr. $$千葉#macross$$' (Gadget M. Chiba, male doctor). The bare token 千葉 stays with the Code Geass pilot 437 CHNN; pilot 436 DSCR uses of $$千葉$$ are correct as they are. The macross brief lists チバソング but not 千葉, so the Macross researcher may not have noticed.
uncertain: FLEIJA: official English is 'F.L.E.I.J.A.' (with periods; franchise wiki, Wikipedia). I set 'FLEIJA' because Jigoku's shipped rt 276 and all three translator proposals use it and periods cost width. Jigoku's own pilot 413 and 418 texts say 'Freya' -- those literal strings in pt_reuse.json should be normalized to the glossary spelling. Orchestrator may choose the dotted form.

Tohdoh vs Todoh: I chose 'Tohdoh' (franchise wiki, akurasu, official). Jigoku shipped rt_reuse 276 has the literal 'Todoh's Zangetsu', which should be fixed to match. Given names: akurasu writes 'Kyoshirou Tohdoh' (Z2 pilot database and the R2 page) and 'Shinichirou Tamaki' (Z2 database) but 'Shinichiro Tamaki' on the R2 page; I used the official 'Kyoshiro' and 'Shinichiro', which match the already-official 'Kallen Kozuki' style. Precedence rule technically favors akurasu's 'Kyoshirou'; orchestrator decides.

Geass Canceller vs Canceler: franchise wiki mostly writes 'Canceler' (one L); Jigoku's shipped text and the official subtitles use 'Canceller'. I kept 'Canceller' (Jigoku precedence, and the wiki does also use it in places).
Cecile: wiki and akurasu write 'Cécile'; I dropped the accent (ASCII-safe, and Jigoku shipped text says 'Cecile'). Ragnarok: same treatment for 'Ragnarök'.

Damocles filed as kind robot (flying fortress = machine) although the rt_259 proposal said keyword; gargantia's Avalon is proposed as keyword. Kind does not change the English; orchestrator may want one convention for fortresses/ships.

特別派遣嚮導技術部 = 'Advanced Special Envoy Engineering Corps' (franchise wiki, the ASEEC name). The game's Japanese has no equivalent of 'Advanced'; I found no separate official English source. Long, but only appears in 'Former chief/member of the X'.
機密情報局 = 'Office of Secret Intelligence' (franchise wiki, Wikipedia); Jigoku's shipped text only says lower-case 'intelligence bureau'. Not verified against the official dub/subtitle script.
Second Battle of Tokyo: wiki page is titled 'Second Assault on Tokyo Settlement'; chose 'Second Battle of Tokyo' (used in wiki prose and in Jigoku shipped text).
In Vogue (two words) corrects the proposals' 'Invogue'; supported by the franchise wiki and Wikipedia.
天子 is a title used as a name: wiki gives her name as Jiang Lihua / 'Tianzi'. Chose 'Tianzi' (Jigoku reference and wiki).
Age mismatches between DSCR and wiki (for example Chiba: DSCR 30, wiki 28/29; Lloyd, Cornelia small differences) are not name issues and were not touched.

Gender for many pilots rests on the franchise wiki because the Japanese DSCR uses no pronouns or gendered nouns (416, 420, 421, 422, 424, 425, 428, 429, 430, 437). Zero (412) is a persona worn by two men; the wiki says 'typically presents as male'.

Source strength: the franchise wiki (codegeass.fandom.com) was read through its MediaWiki API; the akurasu R2 page supplies the cast/unit lists but contains almost no glossary text. No akurasu Tengoku page discusses these names, so nothing here comes from the saved Z3.2 files apart from unit/pilot listings of Zero, Suzaku, Kallen and the two Lancelots.
